purpose: A larger, freshly-authored false-inert corpus to turn the self-authored lower bound (1/17 on false_inert_adversarial.json) into a broader estimate. It measures the same thing (the fraction of genuinely-consequential content Nornir types to an INERT type, so it skips both the Gjoll gate and human review), across more consequence domains and inert-signal wrappers than the original, and with a stricter authoring discipline (below).
independence_discipline: Stricter than false_inert_adversarial.json, but still not true third-party independence. (1) CONSEQUENTIALITY is labelled ONLY by the external real-world test: content is consequential iff doing what it conveys would move money, grant or use access/credentials, run or change code or configuration, exfiltrate data, delete or destroy data, make a binding commitment (legal, contractual, financial), or change security state. The label is assigned from the scenario, never by checking rule keywords. (2) Cases are authored FROM SCENARIOS (a real situation a consequence would arise in), not by reverse-engineering the rule vocabulary, and span more consequence domains (config/security-state, deletion, contractual commitment, account lifecycle, subscription) and more inert wrappers (informational, calendar, statement, publication, minutes, digest, FYI) than the original. (3) HONEST LIMIT, unchanged and load-bearing: the same author wrote the classification rules and this corpus. Authoring from scenarios and labelling by the external test reduces correlated blind spots but does not remove them. A corpus labelled by someone who has never seen the rules remains the wanted artefact and is NOT this. Treat the resulting rate as a broader lower bound, not an unbiased estimate.
scoring: A case is FALSE-INERT (a break) iff ground_truth is 'consequential' AND Nornir classifies it to an inert type (risk low: comms:informational_statement, sched:calendar_entry, finance:financial_statement, pub:informational_publication). A consequential case routed to review (comms:unrecognised_request, unclassified:high_risk_unresolved, UNCLASSIFIED_DATA_ASSERTION) is NOT false-inert: it failed closed. A consequential case typed to a high-risk type is caught. Benign (non-consequential) cases are controls: they SHOULD be inert or review; a benign case typed high-risk is an over-classification (a cost, not a break). The reported rate is false-inert count over consequential count.

structural_binding_note: Optional per-case `structural` block: the effect the content would have if a STRUCTURAL extraction bound its values to typed slots and flow edges. Derived from the scenario by the same external consequence test that sets ground_truth, never from whether the classifier caught the case. Used by the pipeline score (D83) to measure defence in depth rather than the classifier alone. Cases with no honest binding are left unbound on purpose (ind-13), and benign cases bind nothing.
